# Rollcall

> Rollcall scans Wayne State's apps and reports each one's PHP image, Laravel version, auth package and PROCTOR result, checked against the dates in CREED's policy. It keeps a snapshot per scan, so you can see drift and an EOL burn-down.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

> Every app answers "present". The ones on PHP 7.4 answer from the back row.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/site/index.html). It is static, with no build step (see `site/README.md`).
On Citadel, the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/rollcall/blob/HEAD/deploy/) serves it: a Squire kit whose front controller puts `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, serve `site/` directly.

Rollcall is the fleet scanner for the Wayne State application stack. For each app it records the PHP image, the
lowest PHP its `composer.json` allows, the Laravel version, the auth package and its version, and the PROCTOR
result. Then it looks up each version by date in CREED's `policy.json`. It keeps one snapshot per scan, so you can
see drift and an EOL burn-down over time. It prunes old snapshots after the retention window (default 90 days; the
newest one always stays).

Rollcall enforces nothing. It never opens an issue, leaves a comment or deploys anything, and it exits `0` whatever
the fleet looks like. The public report has totals only: counts and progress, no app names, owners or rankings. The
per-app list is internal. Like a good attendance sheet, it is for noticing who is missing, not for shaming them.

Every page below is Markdown. The HTML pages send the same Markdown to a client that asks for `text/markdown`. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit from the README and the pages; do not edit.

## Pages

- [Rollcall: Every app answers present.](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/index.md): Rollcall scans Wayne State's apps and reports each one's PHP image, Laravel version, auth package and PROCTOR result, checked against the dates in CREED's policy. It keeps a snapshot per scan, so you can see drift and an EOL burn-down.
- [How it is built | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/architecture.md): A framework-free core plus thin entry points, a generated copy of CREED's policy reader, and three data sources.
- [Run the checks | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/checks.md): composer ci is the contract, with Docker, pipelines and the front page accessibility gate; Contributing follows.
- [Use Rollcall from your coding agent (ADVISOR) | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.md): Rollcall ships an ADVISOR module with three read-only tools that answer public counts only.
- [Run the collector in Docker | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/collector-docker.md): Build the collector image and run a scan with docker run, with no PHP on the machine.
- [Laravel | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.md): Register the package, publish the config, schedule the scan, and enable the dashboard routes.
- [Metrics | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.md): Metrics are off by default; with ROLLCALL_METRICS_ENABLED=true, /metrics serves Prometheus text from the latest snapshot.
- [Quick start | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.md): Scan and report on the fixtures in the repo, with no network and no token.
- [What the report says | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-the-report-says.md): The sections of a Rollcall report: versions, states, drift kinds, progress and the EOL burn-down.
- [WSU values (Playbook) | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.md): ROLLCALL_GITLAB_URL may come from Playbook when the environment has none; the token never does.
- [Rollcall | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.md): Rollcall is the fleet scanner for the Wayne State application stack.
- [Install | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.md): Install Rollcall from Packagist with one Composer line.
- [Commands | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.md): The rollcall commands, generated from the CLI, with the exit codes and what each one prints.
- [Configuration | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.md): Every Rollcall setting is an environment variable; the table is generated and the GitLab setup follows it.
- [Proof | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.md): Rollcall's first scheduled scan of the stack on GitLab CI, and a rerun over 58 Wayne State applications on 2026-11-06: what ran, what held, what it caught in Rollcall, and what it does not prove yet.
- [Security notes | Rollcall docs](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/docs/security.md): Rollcall is read-only toward every source, keeps the GitLab token out of git and output, and treats scanned files as data.

## Prompts

- [Get started with Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-get-started): Call the sample roll from a checkout, with the bundled fixtures, and have the agent read the report back to you. The prompt itself is in https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Rollcall as a plain PHP tool](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php): The CLI on a schedule, and the /metrics and /report.json front controller only if you ask for them. The prompt itself is in https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [Rollcall in a Laravel app](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel): The scheduled scan and the dashboard of totals. The dashboard is the package's own Blade page, whatever your app renders with. The prompt itself is in https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
